剑16 Test 1 T1.essay:
The line graph tracks the percentage of households owning three electrical appliances, together with the number of hours spent on housework each week, in one country between 1920 and 2019.

It is clear that appliance ownership rose dramatically over the period shown. It is also noticeable that this happened alongside a sharp fall in the time families spent on housework.

The refrigerator saw the most remarkable growth: almost no households owned one in 1920, but the figure climbed to around 45% by 1940 and had reached virtually every home by 1980. Vacuum cleaners followed a similar path, starting at roughly 30% and becoming almost universal after 2000. The washing machine was the slowest of the three, rising only gradually from 40% in 1920 to 75% by the end of the period.

The time devoted to housework fell in step with these changes. It halved from about 50 hours per week in 1920 to 20 hours by 1950, and continued declining to a low of just 10 hours in 2019. The contrast could hardly be clearer: as homes acquired these machines, the household workload shrank to a fifth of its former level.

2.why: 开头改写：shows the changes in ownership→tracks the percentage of households owning（名词改从句）；and连接的「家务时长」补成 the number of hours spent on housework each week——双信息一个不漏；时间段1920-2019原样保留。
2.modelPara: The line graph tracks the percentage of households owning three electrical appliances, together with the number of hours spent on housework each week, in one country between 1920 and 2019.

剑16 Test 2 T1.essay:
The diagram illustrates how sugar is produced from sugar cane in seven distinct stages.

It is clear that the process begins with the growing of the crop and ends with the drying and cooling of the final crystals. It is also noticeable that harvesting can be carried out in two different ways.

The first stage takes place in the fields, where sugar cane needs 12 to 18 months to mature before it is harvested. This can be done either mechanically, with machines cutting the cane, or manually, by farmers using simple tools. The harvested cane is then fed into a crushing mill, which presses it to extract the raw juice.

Preparing the juice for consumption involves the remaining four stages. It is first filtered to remove impurities, before being heated in an evaporator, which turns it into a thick syrup. Next, the syrup passes into a centrifuge, where the sugar crystals are separated from the rest of the liquid. Finally, the crystals are dried and cooled, at which point the sugar is ready for sale.

2.why: 流程图开头：主动改写为被动（making sugar from sugar cane→how sugar is produced from sugar cane），并把步数直接写进开头一句（in seven distinct stages）——流程图题把步数前置，考官一眼确认你看懂了全图。
2.modelPara: The diagram illustrates how sugar is produced from sugar cane in seven distinct stages.

expressions.zh: 糖如何由甘蔗制成（被动改写）

expressions.en: in seven distinct stages
expressions.zh: 分七个明确阶段（步数前置）

3.why: 概括=起终点+分叉点：句1 from growing to drying and cooling 框住全程；句2点出流程里唯一的分支（收割有两种方式）——分支是这张图区别于普通线性流程的最显著特征，必须进overview。

This can be done either mechanically, with machines cutting the cane, or manually, by farmers using simple tools. 剑16 Test 3 T1.chartNote: 地图：Southwest Airport 现状vs明年翻修后。关键变化：登机口8→10；安检口后移；新增bag drop区；连接走廊改为sky train；café扩为café+shop；等待区设施增多。规划图用将来时。
剑16 Test 3 T1.essay:
The plans show the current layout of Southwest Airport and how the site will look once it has been redeveloped next year.

It is clear that the main change will be an increase in the number of gates, from eight to ten. It is also noticeable that passengers will move around the airport in a completely different way after the work is completed.

At present, travellers check in at the entrance area, where security is located, and then walk along a single corridor to reach the eight gates. After redevelopment, this entrance zone will be substantially reorganised: a bag drop will be added beside the check-in desks, the security area will be moved behind them, and the café will be converted into a combined café and shop.

The most striking alteration concerns the walkway. Instead of walking the full length of the building, passengers will board a sky train, which will carry them directly to the gates; two extra gates, including one replacing the existing café, will bring the total to ten, and the waiting area beside them will offer more seats and facilities for the increased number of travellers.

2.why: 规划图地图（现在vs将来）开头：The plans show... and how the site will look——用 will look 一词锁定全文将来时基调；once it has been redeveloped 用完成时讲「翻修完成」这一时点（体系2.1：时态由时间定）。
2.modelPara: The plans show the current layout of Southwest Airport and how the site will look once it has been redeveloped next year.

expressions.en: how the site will look once it has been redeveloped

剑16 Test 4 T1.essay:
The diagram shows the stages by which plastic bottles are recycled, from the moment they are thrown away to the production of new goods.

It is clear that the process consists of nine steps, beginning at the recycling bin and ending with everyday products such as clothing and toys. It is also noticeable that both the public and industrial machinery play essential parts in the cycle.

The first three stages take place before the bottles reach the factory. Consumers drop their used bottles into recycling bins, from which the bottles are collected by lorries and taken to a sorting centre, where reusable bottles are separated from unusable ones. In the preparation stage, the sorted bottles are compressed into large blocks, crushed into small pieces and washed thoroughly.

The manufacturing stage begins when the clean pieces are melted down and formed into pellets. These pellets are then heated once more and rolled into sheets, which are used to make a wide range of end products, from clothes to stationery. What makes this process remarkable is that it never truly finishes: today's plastic bottle becomes part of tomorrow's product, and the cycle can begin again.

2.why: 开头把流程的起终点装进 from...to... 介词短语（from thrown away to production of new goods），一句完成改写+全程框架——比 The diagram shows the process of recycling 更具体。
2.modelPara: The diagram shows the stages by which plastic bottles are recycled, from the moment they are thrown away to the production of new goods.
